blocker: lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex's @markdown_link_pattern regex only matches CommonMark inline link/image syntax [text](url)/![alt](url). It does not match reference-style link/image definitions ([text][ref] ... [ref]: javascript:alert(1)), which any conformant downstream markdown renderer resolves into a real href/src. contains_unsafe_link_scheme?/1 returns false for such payloads (no [...](...) substring exists), so validate_no_unsafe_link_scheme/2 adds no error and the row is written with a javascript: payload live in body -- a complete bypass of REQ-364's own AC2 write-path sanitization requirement.
non_blocking_finding: create_draft/2's `with` has an else clause mapping {:error, :invalid_schema_name} -> {:error, :invalid_prefix}, but update_draft/3, publish/2, reconfirm/2, withdraw/2 have no else clause, so an invalid prefix on those falls through as the raw {:error, :invalid_schema_name} instead of the documented {:error, :invalid_prefix} in their @specs. Not a crash, but a real spec/implementation inconsistency for REVIEWER.
required_fix: Extend the URL-scheme scan to also match reference-style link-definition lines (e.g. ^\s*\[[^\]]+\]:\s*(\S+)), applied post-code-stripping the same way as the existing inline check, OR reconsider design section 5.3 option 2 (a real sanitizer/parser) given a regex denylist over markdown's full link-syntax surface has now demonstrated a concrete gap.
scope_creep_flag_resolved: withdraw/2 (live->draft, added because design section 2's lifecycle diagram shows this transition though REQ-364's acceptance criteria don't name it separately) reviewed for independent security concern -- none found, follows the identical with-chain/prefix-scoping pattern as every other function. Scope-creep question itself deferred to REVIEWER, not a security finding.
